rationale: Sixty-first pass: probe the completion contract of a user-requested snapshot, which the earlier snapshot work only touched from the save-error side. The pending-snapshot object holds one request at a time with a deadline, its gc pass reports a timeout once the logical clock passes that deadline, and a matching apply reports completion, rejection or abort. A focused object-level test asks it four things: whether a request is accepted and left pending, whether it times out, whether the object accepts a new request afterwards, and whether a zero timeout is refused. A first run of the probe read the stale request out of the snapshot channel and failed to complete the second request, which exposed a flaw in the probe rather than in the target; the harness now selects the request whose key matches the pending state and reports the stale entries it skipped. Recording the experiment now so the receipt can be interpreted next.

investigations.question: When a user-requested snapshot is accepted by the pending-snapshot object and never reported back, does the caller receive a terminal result, does the object accept a later request, and what happens to the snapshot request that was already handed to the node?
investigations.hypothesis: An accepted snapshot request stays pending until its deadline passes, at which point the gc pass reports a timeout and clears the slot so a new request is accepted, while the SSRequest already delivered to the node remains queued and its later apply finds no pending state.

scope.description: Probe the pending-snapshot completion contract at the object level: one request that expires, one that completes, and one rejected for a zero timeout.
assumptions: The snapshot channel is a buffered channel that stands in for the node's snapshot request channel, so handing a request over is observable without a node.
The logical clock is advanced explicitly with the object's own tick method, so the deadline is passed deterministically rather than by waiting.
A matching apply is supplied with the key carried by the pending request state, which is the same key written into the snapshot request that was queued.
excluded: Any raft node, snapshotter, state machine or log write; the snapshot is never taken.
Behaviour of a request whose key does not match the pending state, beyond the stale entries the probe consumes while looking for its own request.

experiment.prefix: A pendingSnapshot is created over a buffered rsm.SSRequest channel with the default logical clock. A user-requested snapshot is submitted with a five tick timeout and the channel length, returned state and error are reported; the completed channel is checked before the clock advances; the clock is then advanced to 20 and the gc pass is run, and the completed channel is read again. A second request is submitted with the same timeout, the queued requests are drained until the one whose key matches the new state is found, the number of stale requests is recorded, and a matching apply with value 42 is delivered before the completed channel is read. Finally a request with a zero timeout is submitted.
